## 2026-06-30

### characterization.spectro: AWG channel count decoupled from the max-R search cap

- `_awg_spectrograph_payload` no longer falls back to
  `resolving_power_cap` when `awg_resolving_power` is unset; it now uses a
  fixed `10_000.0` hardware default. `resolving_power_cap` is only the upper
  bound of the `max_spectral_resolution` search, so a deliberately uncapped
  search (e.g. `resolving_power_cap = 1e9`) previously inflated the AWG bin
  grid to ~10^8 bins and allocated tens of GB, OOM-killing CI runners. All
  shipped configs already set `awg_resolving_power` explicitly, so their
  behavior is unchanged.
- Added `test_awg_resolving_power_defaults_independently_of_resolving_power_cap`
  to pin the decoupling.

## 2026-06-12

### Paper bundle: per-planet achievable R and characterization survey table

- `char_max_R` in the paper bundle exoplanet survey is now computed per
  planet: the largest resolving power at which every Nyquist sampled
  spectral bin keeps SNR >= 3 (physics `max_spectral_resolution`, capped
  at the R = 1e4 AWG limit), evaluated through both the
  curve-interpolated and scalar-retune characterization paths.
  Previously the column copied the scene-level `max_spectral_resolution`

  bottom margin caption are removed (the paper figure caption carries
  that information); y-axis floor raised 1e-11 -> 1e-10.

### Chip-opt restart variance tamed: NAYRA tracker floor + KILO throughput penalty

- The ~+/-40% identical-config planet-SNR spread traced to restart-basin
  luck that rank-priority selection could not see: the inherited
  `tracker_observability_min_singular_per_nm = 1e-3` floor sits ~10x below
  the naturally achieved minimum (~1.1e-2 /nm), so `rank_at_floor` is
  always full and the selection key degenerates to objective loss.
- `examples/nayra_eelt.toml` det chip_opt floor raised 1e-3 -> 1.2e-2 /nm,
  just above the achieved minimum. Floor x seed probe
  (examples/test/nayra_eelt_tracker_floor_probe.toml, run 20260612-074332,
  J=5, 3 seeds per floor): seed-to-seed SNR spread 1.60x -> 1.04x, mean
  1347 -> 1447; 3e-2 over-binds (rank 5/17) with no further gain.
- The same floor raise backfires on `examples/kilo_keck_6.toml`: the
  24-mode kernel_order=3 mesh has no DOF slack, so the observability hinge
  sells planet dark throughput (0.068 -> 0.011 in bad cells, J=4 SNR mean
  40 -> 23). There the basin stabilizer is the throughput reward itself:
  `throughput_penalty_alpha` raised 1e-3 -> 1e-2 (floor kept at 1e-3)
  collapses the 3-seed J=4 spread 1.21x -> 1.01x and beats the publication
  chip (run 20260611-083036) at every J: det SNR 40.5 -> 45.3 (J=4),
  6.96 -> 9.33 (J=6), 1.47 -> 1.73 (J=8), 0.173 -> 0.240 (J=10),
  0.0032 -> 0.0039 (J=12); characterization SNR unchanged. Validation
  runs kilo_keck_6_tp_full_{a,b}/20260612-100900; the tp+floor arm (b)
  matched tp-alone at mid-J but lost at J=4 and J=12.
- Probe/validation grids preserved under examples/test/:
  nayra_eelt_tracker_floor_probe, kilo_keck_6_tracker_floor_probe,
  kilo_keck_6_floor_tp_grid, kilo_keck_6_tp_full_{a,b}.

## 2026-06-11

### HWO config modernization; Guyon 2006 ideal-coronagraph overlay

- examples/hwo_space.toml: adopted the `[instrument]` shared port topology
  (36 modes, 10 bright / 26 dark, no spectro) in place of port counts
  repeated across five stages, dropped the vestigial
  `calibration.floor_lookup` stage (the photon-noise baseline imposes no
  floor; performance.standard records the absent floor source), and removed
  the detector `integration_time_s` override now materialized from
  `[observation]`.
- New physics module `nullsim/physics/ideal_coronagraph.py`: the Guyon,
  Pluzhnik, Kuchner, Collins & Ridgway (2006, ApJS 167, 81) theoretically
  optimal coronagraph bound. Planet throughput is the complement of the
  off-axis source's projection onto the removed stellar subspace — the flat
  pupil mode at order 2 (`1 - |2 J1(x)/x|^2`, 50% point near 0.5 lambda/D),
  plus the tip/tilt modes at order 4 (`- |4 J2(x)/x|^2`, 50% point near
  1 lambda/D). Finite-star leakage is the same function area-averaged over
  the uniform disk (small-disk limits x^2/8 and x^4/192), and the 5-sigma
  contrast bound is photon noise on leaked starlight plus backgrounds.
- detection_space plot: opt-in `[output.detection_space]
  ideal_coronagraph_orders = [2, 4]` overlays the bound for the same star,
  aperture, zodi background, integration time, and SNR target as the run,
  but through perfect optics (full clear primary, mirror train, detector
  QE — none of the photonic chain's fiber/chip/polarization losses).
  Single-aperture configs only. hwo_space.toml enables orders 2 and 4; the
  order-2 bound is stellar-size walled on the 1.86 mas solar disk at 5 pc,
  which is the Guyon 2006 argument for the fourth-order null the HWO
  kernel projector enforces.

### NAYRA detection chip rebaselined: kernel_order=2 + heavy disk samples

- Iterative det-chip tuning pass over the J=5 cell
  (examples/test/nayra_eelt_det_tune{1,2,3a,3b}.toml, finalist validation
  nayra_eelt_det_final_k{2,3} runs 20260611-162428) found the
  kernel_order=3 Taylor rows compete with planet routing for the same
  unitary degrees of freedom, capping planet dark throughput at
  0.40-0.45 regardless of throughput_penalty_alpha; second-order rows
  keep ~0.58 while disk_weight=2.0 with 5 rings holds the disk floor
  near 6e-6, below the piston-driven realized null that dominates J>=5.
- examples/nayra_eelt.toml chip_opt: kernel_order 3 -> 2, disk_n_rings
  3 -> 5, disk_weight 1.0 -> 2.0, throughput_penalty_alpha 1e-3 -> 1e-2,
  tracker_observability_crlb_weight 1e-3 -> 1e-1, n_restarts 5 -> 8.
  Validated planet SNR vs the kernel_order=3 baseline (20260611-105935):
  J=5 1565 vs 486, J=9 112 vs 72, J=3 1769 vs 3250 (the old J=3 cell's
  deep disk floor plus a lucky tracker draw stays unbeaten);
  characterization SNR is best-of-any-chip at J>=5 because the spectro
  realized floor inherits the detection chip's servo bandwidth.
- Known issue recorded in the config: identical-config chip draws still
  spread ~+/-40% in SNR because tracker_observability_min_singular_per_nm
  = 1e-3 never binds, so rank-priority restart selection degenerates to
  objective loss. Raising the floor until it discriminates is the open
  variance lever.

### NAYRA detection chip adopts the KILO kernel-null recipe

- examples/nayra_eelt.toml chip_opt: `kernel_order` 0 -> 3, `disk_n_rings`
  1 -> 3, `disk_weight` 0.01 -> 1.0, matching the kilo_keck.toml production

---

### NAYRA N=18 quadrature modernization; dual-pol diagnostics; KILO dual-pol chain

- examples/nayra_eelt.toml: overhauled from the legacy N=48 classic-mesh
  config to N=18 on the modern architecture — duplicated-input quadrature
  mesh (18 physical modes -> 36 Clements inputs, 18 tracker + 17 dark +
  1 spectro), dual-pol PBS front end with `deployment_mode="per_pol_arm"`,
  photometric amplitude pickoff, photon-Kalman fringe tracking (no
  inter-telescope/vibration terms: single bench), `[instrument]`
  materialization replacing the ~25 zipped port-count sweep axes, full
  20-bin compiled characterization objectives, and the modern
  evidence-based values (predictive gain x3, amp servo gain 3.0, chip
  insertion loss -2 dB, auto setpoint trim). The unused
  `calibration.floor_lookup` stage is dropped.
- Single-aperture piston routing: the photon-Kalman FT charges tracker
  measurement noise to a rank-1 inter-telescope common mode, so
  `sensitivity.detection_curve` with `ao_piston_residual_source =
  "opd_budget"` raises on n_apertures = 1. NAYRA sources its realized
  piston covariance from the bright-port CRLB instead
  (`ao_piston_residual_source="fringe_observability"` with the
  temporal-Kalman model; diagnostics stage moved before sensitivity).
  Any single-aperture config must follow the same pattern.
- diagnostics.fringe_observability: dual-pol support. The chip-input
  recovery uses the dominant-power PBS arm's coherent response (the arms
  share the design unitary with small per-arm trims, so fractional piston
  responses agree to first order); detector rate rows are arm-summed and
  per-arm port labels collapsed to physical chip ports, driven by the
  detector-published `n_pol_arms`. Count budgets therefore include both
  arms. Tests pin dual-pol == arm-summed single-pol CRLB.
- examples/kilo_keck_6.toml: the canonical KILO config now carries the
  physical dual-polarization chain (HWP + PBS + PM980 Jones propagation,
  chip deployed per PBS arm) with the hardware values from KILO
  PBSConfig/HWPConfig/PMFiberConfig. The original KILO code's
  `PolarizationMode` defaulted to SCALAR_LEGACY, so the paperv3 products
  and the parity parent `kilo_keck.toml` remain scalar; kilo_keck_6
  results now include PBS/HWP losses and polarization leakage terms and
  will not match the scalar parity targets exactly.
- fringe_tracking.closed_loop: the tracker photon budget pools the
  per-arm detector channels of each physical bright port (both arms see
  the same piston fringe) instead of treating each channel as its own
  estimator — per-channel division doubled the assumed shot variance in
  dual-pol pipelines. The per-port SNSPD capacity scales with the arm
  count (one tracker detector set per arm chip). The detector
  `n_pol_arms` lookup is now the shared `stages._utils.detector_n_pol_arms`,
  reused by the fringe-observability diagnostic.
- background.sky_surface_brightness in dual-pol configs: per-port sky
  etendue set to `n_polarizations = 1` (each PBS-arm waveguide accepts a
  single polarization). Downstream consumers multiply the per-port rate
  by the per-arm detector channel count, so the scalar default of 2
  double-counted the sky background in dual-pol pipelines (both
  kilo_keck_6 and nayra_eelt; the legacy NAYRA N=48 dual-pol runs carried
  the same 2x sky overcount).
- Tracker detector capacity: `_SNSPD_MAX_RATE_HZ` corrected from 2.5e7 to
  the 1e8 cps device capability (matching the detector.snspd stage
  default); SNSPDs gang per port via `tracker_n_detectors_per_port`.
  NAYRA budgets 16 ganged SNSPDs per port per arm (3.2e9 cps/port) in
  both the FT budget and the fringe-observability channel cap — the old
  1e8 channel cap clipped 16/36 arm channels at J=3, and with the N=18
  piston floor coming from the tracker CRLB the bright cells were
  capacity-limited, not photon-limited (J=3 scored below J=5).
  kilo_keck_6's diagnostic channel cap is raised to 8e8 to match its
  4-SNSPD-per-arm FT budget. Dark/spectro ports remain ganged MKIDs
  (1e5 cps/pixel), splittable with photonic power dividers; their pools
  were not near saturation in either config.

## 2026-06-10

### Photon-limited auto setpoint trim

The fixed 2.5 nm dark-port trim dither and 1.0 nm setpoint placeholders are
replaced by a derived joint optimum: the 1f lock-in signal scales as
dither x offset, so the held setpoint goes as 1/dither and the total added
leakage L(A) = G A^2/2 + n G (k/A)^2 minimizes at A_opt^4 = 2 n k^2 with
equal dither/bias partition (physics.fringe_tracking.photon_limited_
setpoint_trim). sensitivity.detection_curve gains auto_setpoint_trim /
trim_loop_bandwidth_hz / n_trim_modes and derives both terms from the
run's detected stellar rate and dark-port floor, so the faint-end budget
degrades honestly as 1/sqrt(flux). kilo_keck J=4: trim leakage 4.6e-5 ->
2.8e-6 (0.47 nm RMS dither), SNR back above the pre-realism baseline.

---

### Characterization curve: full-wavelength-grid retune objective

The 5-sample broadband objective aliased the planet's chromatic phase
winding (>1 cycle across the J band beyond ~15-20 mas), so outer
characterization anchors collapsed ~50-1000x in contrast relative to
detection mode. The kilo_keck_6 characterization_curve stage now optimizes
on the full 20-bin grid: the smooth landscape lets 3 restarts find the good
basin (31 mas anchor: contrast 7.7e-8 vs 6.7e-5; 10 restarts at 5 samples
only reached 1.4e-7). Char mode now tracks and beats detection mode from
the IWA to near the OWA.

---

### Characterization SNR proxy saturates at the null floor

The characterization optimizer's in-loop SNR proxy rewarded static stellar
leak as `sqrt(null_floor / leak)` with the clamp at `null_floor * 1e-12`,
so driving leak three decades below the floor multiplied the reward ~30x
even though the deployed leak is pinned at the realized piston floor
(~3e-6). The optimizer traded planet throughput for un-cashable null
depth: wide characterization-curve anchors landed at 0.04-0.19 spectro
throughput with ~1e-9 static leak. The proxy now clamps at `null_floor`
(matching the restart-selection score), so below-floor leak earns nothing
and the remaining gradient goes to throughput. kilo_keck_6 J=4 anchors:
17.7 mas throughput 0.042 -> 0.409, 31.2 mas 0.072 -> 0.701; contrast
improves 4-7x over 15-100 mas, putting char mode decisively below
detection mode where it should be.

`examples/kilo_keck_6.toml`: the `characterization` spectro stage now uses
the full 20-bin broadband objective (`broadband_n_wavelengths = 20`). The
old single-design-bin economy produced chips with ~5e-4 mean broadband
leak (restart selection evaluated the full grid but only ever saw
chromatically optimized candidates); headline `char_snr` at J=4 rises
12.9 -> 134.6 and `char_leakage_rate_hz` falls 345 kHz -> 3.6 kHz.

---

### Classical fringe tracker: shot noise no longer capped at the open-loop budget

The KILO-heritage cap of the full classical residual at the open-loop AO
total hid the sensor shot noise once it exceeded the atmospheric budget
(between J=8 and J=10): the published residual understated J=12 by ~7x in
rms and the sample-rate optimizer's iid term went rate-independent, pinning
the bandwidth at sample_rate_max while still claiming full common-mode
rejection. The raw lag + shot + uncorrectable + irreducible sum is now
published; the numeric optimizer trades shot noise against disturbance
rejection honestly (a starved loop slows down), and the diagnostic flag is
renamed shot_exceeds_open_loop. The photon-Kalman branch was never
affected (its shot noise enters through the uncapped CRLB path).

---

Fixes for the 2026-06-10 deep review (`reviews/kilo_keck_6-sweep-2026-06-10.md`).
Correctness:

- background: sky étendue is scaled by n_physical/n_chip modes after the

- fringe tracking: photon-Kalman `f_sample_hz` publishes the real loop

## 2026-06-09

### Stage cache: config_hash-independent keys (Tier 3)

A stage's cache key no longer folds in the global `config_hash` unless the
stage actually draws from the `config_hash`-seeded `context.rng`
(`uses_rng=True` — only `transport.smf28`/`pm980`/`pm780` and
`background.space_zodi`). Every other stage's result is `config_hash`-
independent, so its key now depends only on its own params, the content digest
of its consumed + `cache_key_extras` budgets, the run-global wavelength grid,
the per-family source digest, and instance identity. Editing one part of a
config (e.g. a `sensitivity` piston param) now **reuses** the cached results of
the expensive `chip_optimization`/`characterization` stages instead of busting
the whole pipeline — turning a ~34 min config re-run into minutes.

`config_hash` was a global catch-all, so removing it required closing the
dependencies it was masking (audited across every stage):

- **The wavelength grid** (`[grid]`) is a run-global input in no stage's
  Params; it is now folded into every stage's cache key directly, so a grid
  edit still invalidates all wavelength-indexed results.
- **`cache_key_extras`** added for stages that read undeclared upstream state:
  `injection.ideal` (`throughput`), `wavefront.space_residual` (`wavefront`,
  `opd_budget`), `telescope.fixed_aperture` (`throughput`),
  `fringe_tracking.closed_loop` (`scene`, `field`).

The per-stage RNG derivation (`derive_rng`) is **unchanged**, so no stochastic
result is re-seeded — the contrast and characterization curves are unaffected.
Verified end-to-end that a cached run after an upstream config edit matches a
fresh no-cache run (no stale results).

---

### Stage cache: source digest excludes output and CLI code

The stage cache source digest (`_compute_package_source_digest`, folded into
every stage's cache key) now excludes all of `nullsim/outputs/**` and the CLI
entry points (`cli.py`, `__main__.py`) — not just `outputs/plots/**` and
`outputs/tables/**` as before. These modules run after the pipeline has
produced `SimulationState` and never feed back into a stage's result, so
editing a plot, table, the paper bundle writer, or the CLI no longer
invalidates the cached (often multi-hour) det/char unitary optimizations.

The exclusion is centralized in a single `_affects_stage_state` predicate
shared by both the digest and the mtime-memoization scan, so the two cannot
drift (a stricter mtime filter would miss edits and serve a stale digest).
Everything that can run during stage execution — pipeline, config, physics,
stages, catalogs — is still hashed conservatively, so any edit that could
change a stage result still busts the cache.

---

### Stage cache: key digests the full input state (sweep-cell state resurrection fix)

The Tier 3 config_hash-independent cache key digested only the stage's
consumed budgets while a cache hit restores the entire pickled post-stage
state. In a parallel sweep, a stage that does not consume `scene` (e.g.
`atmosphere.kolmogorov`) had identical keys across cells, so one cell's full
state — `scene.star_jmag` included — was resurrected into every other cell,
poisoning all downstream photon budgets and silently skipping the
characterization stages (every cell believed it was J=6). `key_for` now
digests the full input state; the redundant `cache_key_extras`/grid folds
were removed; regression tests reproduce the sweep poisoning end-to-end.

---

### Stage cache: per-family source digest (Tier 2 granularity)

The stage cache source digest is now computed per stage family instead of over
the whole package. A stage's cache key folds in the shared core (pipeline,
config, physics, catalogs, the shared `stages/_*.py` helpers) plus the
transitive import closure of the stage's own family over other stage families.
Output and CLI code remain excluded (Tier 1).

Effect: editing one stage family's code no longer invalidates the cached
(often multi-hour) optimizations of unrelated families. The det path
(`chip_optimization`, `sensitivity`) imports no part of the char path, so
editing `characterization` reuses the det cache and editing `sensitivity`
reuses the char cache. Editing genuinely shared code (e.g. `chip_optimization`
— which `characterization` and `chip` import — or anything under `physics/`)
still correctly busts every dependent family.

The family-import closure is derived from the AST of each family's modules
(real import statements only, never docstring mentions), so it stays correct as
dependencies change with no hand-maintained dependency map — and it already
caught a real `chip_optimization` → `delay_lines.geometric` edge that manual
greps missed. Any ambiguity (unparseable file, unresolved relative import,
unknown stage family) falls back to including every family, so the digest can
only over-invalidate, never serve a stale result. The digest and the
mtime-memoization scan share the `_affects_stage_state` filter so they cannot
drift.

---

### Characterization stages: torch.compile support, systematic-eps consistency, and null_floor emission

Both `characterization.spectro` and `characterization.detection_curve` now
accept a `compile_objective` param (bool, default false) that gates
`torch.compile` on the characterization optimizer objective. The env var
`NULLSIM_TORCH_COMPILE` is also honored. When compilation is on, restarts are
forced to serial to avoid concurrent JIT contention.

Both stages also gain `eps_calibration_residual` and
`residual_speckle_stability_factor` params (mirroring `performance.standard`).
These combine via `_combined_systematic_eps` into a single `eps_systematic`
value that is used consistently through the optimization and SNR calculation,
replacing the previous ad-hoc treatment.

Both stages now emit `eps_systematic` and `null_floor` in their results
payloads, making the realized systematic budget inspectable in
`sweep_results.parquet` and the paper bundle.

### Parallel sweep: coordinated intra-op thread budget

`nullsim run` with multiple sweep workers now sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS`,
`MKL_NUM_THREADS`, and `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS` to `cores / n_workers` before
spawning the process pool. This prevents torch / BLAS from defaulting to a
full-core thread pool inside each worker and oversubscribing the host. An
explicit user setting for any of these variables is left untouched
(`os.environ.setdefault`).

---

### Debug report: FT disturbance panel, null waterfall terms, assumptions page

The fringe-tracking page now shows the control model, f_sample vs f_3dB (or
the photon-Kalman window/equivalent bandwidth), the estimation/prediction/
line-floor and IID-vs-common residual decomposition, the live disturbance
inputs (Greenwood effective wind vs configured, von Karman sigma and PSD
knee, post-feedforward vibration line spectrum, fused broadband floor), and
the OPD supersession list. The null waterfall adds setpoint-trim and dither
leakage bars plus the eps_systematic/NSC composition, and the report ends
with a live-valued assumptions-and-limits page.

---

### kilo_keck_6: realistic det piston floor + restore the char-mode curve

Two regressions in the kilo_keck_6 detection-space figure (both dating to the
June 5-8 work) are fixed.

**Det null was ~10x too shallow.** The `sensitivity` stage was using the
fringe-observability temporal-Kalman `one_step_prediction` piston surrogate
(~3.1 nm at J=4 / 6.3 nm at J=8), which was built on the *open-loop* AO prior
(10.4 nm) and used the closed-loop servo bandwidth (11.5 Hz) as the prediction
interval, overestimating the piston ~4x. The config now uses
`ao_piston_residual_source = "opd_budget"`, i.e. the actual closed-loop
`fringe_tracking.closed_loop` residual (~0.71 nm at J=4 / 3.94 nm at J=8), which
restores a floor-limited null (~1e-5 at J=4). The `fringe_observability` stage
still runs for the single-frame CRLB / observability diagnostics. Applied to
both `examples/kilo_keck_6.toml` and `examples/test/kilo_keck_6.toml`.

**Char-mode curve collapsed to ~2 points.** `detection_space`'s char-curve
plotter gated anchors on a second, stricter `full_band_constraint_margin`
(static null <= null_floor across every detector bin) that the optimizer never
targeted — it nulls to `null_floor` only on the broadband design grid. That
dropped 8 of 12 feasible anchors. The plot now gates only on
`optimization_constraint_margin_per_anchor` (the margin the optimizer actually
solved against), restoring the full characterization curve. Anchors that fail
the optimizer's own constraint are still dropped.

---

### Paper-deliverable presentation fixes

Four follow-on fixes to how characterization and fringe-tracking results are
presented in the paper bundle:

* **Fringe-observability figure.** The summary panel now distinguishes the
  single-frame CRLB observability ("CRLB RMS (1 frame)" / "Trunc. CRLB
  (1 frame)") from the realized piston floor that actually enters the contrast
  curve ("Realized floor (temporal)"). The realized value is sourced from the
  `sensitivity.detection_curve` `ao_piston_residual` (covariance-resolved, then
  temporal-Kalman selected, then scalar-resolved). Previously the figure
  headlined the ~0.17 nm CRLB while the operative floor was the ~3 nm
  temporal-lag value, with nothing linking them.

* **Characterization throughput columns.** `char_spectro_throughput`
  (performance_summary) and `spectro_throughput` (characterization_summary) are
  renamed to `*_design_bin` to make explicit that they are the chip efficiency
  at the single design wavelength, and a `*_band_avg` column (mean of the
  per-wavelength planet throughput) is added — the bandwidth-consistent figure
  alongside the band-integrated characterization SNR.

* **Skipped characterization-curve cells.** When a run produces
  separation-resolved characterization curves for some cells but skips others
  (`skip_jmags`), the paper exoplanet survey no longer falls back to the
  single-scene scalar retune SNR for the skipped cells (which is not valid at
  arbitrary planet separations). Those planets keep their detection-mode rates
  but report NaN characterization SNR.

* **Host disk column.** `host_disk_mas` is renamed to `assumed_star_disk_mas`.
  The bundled catalog snapshot carries no per-host stellar radius, so the floor
  is computed for the single configured scene star and applied to every overlay
  planet; the column is the assumed reference disk, not each host's true
  angular diameter.

---

### Characterization stellar-rate parity: injection coupling now folded into rate reconstruction

`injection.ideal` and `injection.single_mode_fiber` carry their fiber-coupling
loss in the field amplitudes (`E = √(η) · …`), recording the coupling spectrum
as a throughput component for provenance. Those components are now flagged
`field_amplitude_applied = True`. Stages that reconstruct an absolute stellar
rate from the throughput budget (`characterization.spectro`) fold the coupling
back in; the detector path is unaffected (it reads the top-level
`transmission_fraction`, which excludes the coupling, and gets it from
`|field|²`).

Previously the characterization stellar rate omitted injection coupling,
inflating `detected_stellar_rate_hz` — and therefore characterization SNR — by
`√(1/η_inj)`. Because `η_inj` tracks AO Strehl, the bias grew toward faint
guide stars (≈1.6× rate error at J=4 rising to ≈24× at J=12 for the KILO Keck
N=6 quadrature config), making faint-end characterization curves optimistic.

### Temporal-Kalman piston: unobserved modes carry full process variance

`temporal_kalman_piston_covariance` no longer skips modes with a zero
measurement eigenvalue. An unobserved differential-piston mode is uncorrected,
so its one-step prediction now carries the full process variance
`prior_variance · (1 − ρ²)` instead of zero. The common-piston mode (zero
baseline) is still excluded. Dormant for full-rank trackers; corrects an
optimistic piston floor for any rank-deficient (sparse-bright-port) tracker.

### Paper bundle fixes

* The PDI survey table now sorts by the SNR metric it displays
  (`snr_pdi_continuous_4h`), with non-finite/missing values sunk to the bottom,
  so the top-of-table LaTeX/JSON selections are consistent and NaN rows no
  longer displace finite ones. The full CSV/JSON exports still retain every
  planet.
* `null_transmission_map` `.npz` archives now also save display-ready
  (East-left) `design_map_display` / `band_averaged_map_display` arrays
  consistent with `display_x_mas` and the plotted PDF; the raw maps remain in
  native (RA-increasing) orientation paired with `l_coords_mas`. A naive
  re-plot from the archive no longer mirrors the figure.
* Removed the dead `detection_space_cache.json` sidecar request from the paper
  `detection_space` product (the plot never wrote it; it was recorded as
  skipped in `paper_manifest.json`).

---

### Stage cache: core-reachable stage families

The stage cache now scans cache-relevant non-stage package code for imports
into `nullsim.stages.<family>`. Any stage family reachable from shared core
code, such as the `physics` to `chip_optimization` edge, is folded into every
stage source digest so shared-core imports cannot serve stale cached results.

---

### Delay lines: phase-reference residual slope

`delay_lines.geometric` now models `phase_reference` chromatic residuals with
the post-reference residual slope `(n_g - n_phi) / c`. Group-delay compensation
and GVD curvature are unchanged.

---

### Fringe tracking: supersede replaced AO piston terms

`fringe_tracking.closed_loop` now supersedes the atmospheric piston and all
AO piston sub-budget components it replaces (`ao_temporal`, `ao_fitting`, and
`ao_wfs_noise`) before rebuilding the active OPD quadrature total.

---

### AO and fringe tracking: effective wind from tau0

Added the Greenwood/Fried `tau0 = 0.314 r0 / v_bar` helper and made
`ao.pyramid_wfs` derive its temporal-lag wind speed from `tau0_500nm_s` by
default. The AO payload now publishes `effective_wind_speed_m_s`, which
`fringe_tracking.closed_loop` uses for its Conan piston frequency when present.

---

### Performance and characterization: remove hand-tuned eps calibration

Removed the `eps_calibration_residual` parameter from performance,
characterization, tests, and examples. Systematic eps is now the quadrature of
the physical null-instability term and the residual speckle-stability factor.

---

### Fringe tracking: inter-telescope piston + vibration disturbances

`nullsim.physics.fringe_tracking` gains pure primitives for the uncorrected
inter-telescope differential piston and the post-servo vibration residual:
`von_karman_differential_piston_rms_m` (B -> L0 saturation, Absil et al. 2006 /
Linfield et al. 2001), `piston_psd_knee_hz` (outer-scale and aperture-averaging
cutoffs, Conan et al. 1995 / Kellerer & Tokovinin 2007),
`servo_residual_variance_flat_knee` (the closed-form 7/12 flat-knee / f^(-17/3)
rejection integral), and `vibration_residual_rms_nm` (per-line `(f/f_c)^2`
rejection plus a flat broadband floor). Derivations and the citation list live
in `tests/physics/notes/fringe_disturbances.md`.

`fringe_tracking.closed_loop` integrates these disturbances behind opt-in Params
(`inter_telescope_piston`, `vibration_line_frequencies_hz`,
`vibration_line_rms_nm`, `vibration_broadband_rms_nm`, `outer_scale_m`,
`servo_bandwidth_fraction`, `sample_rate_max_hz`). The stage now separates the
detector sample rate from the closed-loop 3 dB bandwidth
(`f_3db = servo_bandwidth_fraction * f_sample`), scales the photon residual by
the closed-loop noise bandwidth (reproducing the prior pi/2 shot term exactly at
`servo_bandwidth_fraction = 0.5`), and, when `servo_bw_hz` is unset, grid-scans
the sample rate (logspace 20 Hz .. `sample_rate_max_hz`, 241 points) over the
full residual budget. The disturbances are tracked as a common differential mode
(`residual_common_differential_nm`) separate from the per-mode IID residual
(`residual_iid_per_mode_nm`), with `outer_scale_m` materialized from
`site.atmosphere.L0_m`. `predictive_lag_reduction` default changed 0.05 -> 0.33.

### Realized-null MC: rank-1 inter-telescope common-mode piston covariance

`nullsim.physics.realized_null` gains `piston_covariance_with_common_mode_m2`,
a per-mode covariance with an IID AO diagonal plus a rank-1 inter-telescope mode
along the +/-1 telescope-sign direction. `sensitivity.detection_curve`'s
`opd_budget` piston path now reads the fringe-tracking IID / common split and,
when the common term is positive, routes a physical-mode covariance through the
existing realized-null covariance MC (mirroring the fringe-observability splitter
handling) so the common differential piston does not average down across modes.

---

### KILO Keck config: Phase B fringe-tracking wiring

`examples/kilo_keck.toml` now enables the photon-Kalman fringe-tracking control
model with inter-telescope piston, Keck vibration lines, accelerometer fusion,
and SNSPD tracker multiplicity. The Phase B science-stage mitigation knobs are
also wired: dark-port setpoint trim leakage in sensitivity and photon-resolved
NSC reduction for performance and characterization.

`examples/kilo_keck_6.toml` drops the unused pre-sensitivity
`fringe_observability` stage and relies on the OPD-budget branch that already
returns before reading fringe-observability payloads.

---

### Phase B controls: photon-Kalman FT, setpoint trim, and NSC

`nullsim.physics.fringe_tracking` now includes the Phase B photon-counting
control primitives: `PhotonKalmanResidual`, `piston_structure_function_m2`,
`fusion_effective_broadband_rms_m`, and `photon_kalman_residual_budget`. The
budget stays frequency-domain: it trades continuous-time photon-estimation
noise against structure-function prediction error plus tracked-line residual
floors, without introducing a time-domain simulator.

`fringe_tracking.closed_loop` gained `control_model = "photon_kalman"`. In
that mode the stage derives an equivalent `f_3db_hz` from the photon-Kalman
window, reports the matching `f_sample_hz`, and publishes the estimation,
prediction, and line-floor decomposition alongside the existing IID/common
piston residual split.

`sensitivity.detection_curve` now charges dark-port setpoint trim leakage via
`null_setpoint_residual_nm` and `setpoint_dither_rms_nm`, and publishes the
resulting leakage terms. `performance.standard`,
`characterization.spectro`, and `characterization.detection_curve` now accept
`nsc_systematic_reduction`, which reduces only the null-instability systematic
term; mean-leakage photon noise is unchanged.

---

### Characterization outputs: rename `feasible` -> `converged`

The characterization summary table column `feasible` is now `converged`, the
`performance_summary` column `char_feasible` is now `char_converged`, and the
helpers `_characterization_payload_is_feasible` (tables) and
`_characterization_component_is_feasible` (paper bundle) are now
`_characterization_payload_converged` and
`_characterization_component_converged`. The logic is unchanged: it reports
optimizer convergence (success plus null-constraint margin within tolerance),
which is what the flag has always measured. The per-anchor curve feasibility
masks (`_characterization_curve_feasible_mask`) are a distinct quantity and are
left as-is.

---

### Chip optimizer: honest disk-floor presentation under flux-dependent objectives

The chip-optimizer disk-floor scatter across the J sweep was traced to the
objective, not a bug. The base broadband null objective (absolute dark-port
leakage plus the throughput penalty) is scale-equivariant: the reported null
depth and the stellar-disk null floor it drives are flux-scale invariant (pinned
in `tests/stages/chip_optimization/test_scale_invariance.py`). The tracker,
joint, and amplitude observability terms, however, carry absolute physical
targets — the per-nm intensity-response singular floor and the CRLB targets in
nm — that are genuinely photon-rate dependent (a fringe tracker's piston
estimability scales with the actual photon flux). When those terms are active
the optimum, and hence the realized disk floor, depends on the flux the chip
was optimized at.

Rather than forcing a normalization that would corrupt the photon-rate-dependent
CRLB targets, this surfaces the dependence honestly:
`ChipOptimizationParams.objective_is_flux_scale_dependent` reports whether any
observability term is active; the chip-optimization payload now carries
`disk_null_floor_note` ("chip-realization dependent" or "flux-scale invariant");
the `ChipOptimizationTorch` docstring names the intentionally scale-dependent
terms; and `performance_summary` now emits `disk_null_floor` and
`disk_null_floor_note` columns so the per-flux disk-floor spread is visible
across sweep cells.

---

### Sensitivity publishes effective leakage rates alongside static-chip rates

`sensitivity.detection_curve` now records three new payload keys when an
upstream detector stage is present: `leakage_rate_hz_effective`
(`effective_null_with_disk` times the bright + dark + spectro stellar rate
total, the same normalization `performance.standard` uses for SNR),
`leakage_rate_hz_static_chip` (the detector dark-port total, i.e. the static
chip null), and `effective_to_static_leakage_ratio`. When no detector
component is present (standalone smoke tests) all three are `None`. The
`debug_report` detector/performance page now prints both leakage truths on one
line, labeling the realized value as the one SNR uses. This resolves the
two-truths artifact where the detector-stage dark rate and the realized
sensitivity leakage looked like a discrepancy.

---

### Project baselines onto the sky plane for off-zenith pointing

`nullsim.physics.uv_coverage` gains `project_positions_to_sky_plane_m`, which
projects ENU aperture positions onto the plane perpendicular to the line of
sight (axis 0 toward increasing azimuth, axis 1 toward increasing altitude).
Off-zenith, baselines foreshorten as seen from the source, so the planet phase
rows `2*pi/lambda * (x*alpha + y*beta)` are only valid after this projection;
at altitude 90 deg / azimuth 0 it is the identity on (East, North).

Stages that feed `aperture_positions_pupil_m` into sky-angle phase rows now
project at their boundary using `scene.altitude_deg` / `scene.azimuth_deg`
(identity when both are unset, preserving zenith configs):
`sensitivity.detection_curve`, the `chip_optimization.scipy` / `.torch`
kernel and disk rows, `chip_optimization.ideal_kernel` kernel-derivative rows,
and the shared `characterization.spectro` / `characterization.detection_curve`
position reader. The projection lives in the new
`nullsim.stages._utils.project_aperture_positions_for_pointing` boundary
helper so the physics primitives stay state-free. The fringe-observability
piston Jacobians are internal OPD responses, not sky angles, and are left
unprojected. `outputs/plots/null_transmission_map` already projects via its
own richer equatorial HA/Dec path and is unchanged.

---

### Sky background: single-mode etendue default; drop unconsumed exozodi

`background.sky_surface_brightness` now defaults the sky spaxel to the
single-mode receiver etendue `Omega = n_polarizations * lambda^2 / A_per_mode`
(new `n_polarizations: int = 2` param) instead of the fixed 0.005 arcsec^2
table, which under-counted the sky by ~4-9x for Keck-scale subapertures. The
per-mode collecting area is the value the stage already derives for the rate
computation, and the band-center wavelength sets `lambda`. An explicit
`spaxel_arcsec2` override still wins; the legacy `DEFAULT_SPAXEL_ARCSEC2` table
remains only as a documented fallback for when the per-mode area is
unavailable. The payload records `spaxel_source` and `n_polarizations` for
audit. `background.nayra_sky` is unchanged.

The unconsumed `[scene.exozodi]` block was removed from
`examples/kilo_keck.toml` (and thus from `kilo_keck_6.toml`, which extends it):
exozodi is only read by `background.space_zodi` on the HWO space path.

---

### Config: `[instrument]` port-topology section

Added a strict top-level `[instrument]` section for shared chip/input-mode and
port-count topology. The loader materializes those values into port-bearing
stages while preserving explicit stage-level overrides. The root KILO Keck
configs now declare the 48-port and 24-port layouts once and rely on
materialization for chip, detector, sensitivity, characterization, injection,
and fringe-tracking stage params.

---

## 2026-05-28

### MKID energy resolution

Added opt-in MKID finite energy-resolution redistribution and MKID-native
spectrograph accounting for `characterization.spectro`. Default MKID detector
runs continue to emit the existing detector payload when
`resolving_power_ref` is unset.

## 2026-05-21

### Added

- Added opt-in chip chromaticity controls shared by chip deployment and
  chip optimization: parametric splitter-angle drift and fixed-OPD
  phase-shifter dispersion, with legacy KILO/NAYRA behavior preserved by
  default.

---

### Changed

- Switched the HWO example from achromatic ideal-kernel deployment to a
  signed-real physical Clements fixed-OPD chip deployment for finite-bandwidth
  evaluation.

---

### Added

- Added an HWO-oriented `chip_optimization.ideal_kernel` stage and a torch
  `warm_start_source` path so finite-bandwidth physical Clements refinements
  can start from the ideal order-3 kernel instead of a cold random basin.

---

### Changed

- Tightened the HWO first-pass physics path: the 24-mode pupil surrogate can
  preserve the full 8 m collecting area while normalizing its maximum baseline
  to the primary diameter, and the HWO config now uses that mode.
- Removed the nonideal PM-fiber Jones/PER degradation from the photon-limited
  HWO baseline while retaining PM780 propagation loss and the dual-PBS-arm chip
  deployment.
- `performance.standard` now bounds sensitivity-stage null floors by the
  detector/calibration residual and uses sensitivity-stage planet throughput at
  the configured planet separation for headline SNR and integration time.
- Added an I-band Vega zero point and opt-in detector-side J-to-band color
  conversion so the 0.8 um HWO config no longer uses the Y/J photometry
  placeholder; KILO/NAYRA detector configs retain the legacy direct-J behavior.

---

### Config

- Update `examples/hwo_space.toml` to model a single 8 m unobstructed HWO
  primary with a photon-noise-limited first-pass baseline.
- Materialize `[telescope.aperture].obscuration_fraction` into
  `injection.single_mode_fiber` so fiber coupling uses the same telescope
  source of truth as the aperture and ideal-injection stages.
- Add `telescope.pupil_modes` and wire HWO through `sensitivity.detection_curve`
  so detection-space plots use separation-dependent planet throughput instead
  of the flat performance fallback.
- Allow detection-space planet overlays to opt into all-sky observability for
  space telescopes instead of inheriting the Mauna Kea altitude cut.
- Give the HWO config an explicit 1-500 mas sensitivity grid and request all
  registered diagnostic plots for debugging.
- Move the first-pass HWO pupil surrogate from 2 modes to 12 modes and let
  `subaperture_layout` read `telescope.pupil_modes` when no AO stage exists.
- Use the torch chip optimizer for the 12-mode HWO exploratory run because
  scipy finite-difference gradients scale poorly at 144 chip parameters.
- Set the HWO default grid to 0.8 µm with 10% bandwidth and use a
  `2 bright + 10 dark` port split for the 12-mode surrogate.
- Model the HWO front end as a KILO/NAYRA-style dual-polarization path:
  PBS split, 2 m PM780 transport, PM-fiber Jones/PER loss, and two physical

- Prevent duplicate Ruilier-Cassaing injection coupling when an
  `injection.ideal` seed stage is followed by `injection.single_mode_fiber`.

docs: sync SPEC.md with removal of frozen parity test suite (commit 7ed7591). Remove dead references to frozen reference JSONs, generate_*_reference.py scripts, CI parity job, and KILO-reference overlays in debug_report description. Update §2, §3, §5, §11, and §12 to describe current test structure (structure/sanity tests) and known physics gaps (without frozen references).

## 2026-05-20

### AWG spectrograph path

Added AWG spectroscopy primitives for Nyquist bin counts, wavelength grids, and
per-bin photon-rate/SNR spectra with throughput and free-spectral-range losses.
The `characterization.spectro` stage now reports a nested rate-binned AWG
spectrum plus headline AWG scalars without changing its existing broadband SNR
or maximum-resolving-power outputs.

The KILO and NAYRA example configs now declare explicit high-resolution AWG
settings for their spectro characterization stages.

---

### Batched torch MZI solver

Added an explicit `torch_device` selector for the torch chip optimizer and a
batched real/imag Clements unitary builder. The torch backend now evaluates
broadband wavelength stacks through the batched builder and uses the same path
to publish the deployed chromatic `optimal_u_stack`, giving CUDA runs a larger
per-step workload while preserving the existing BFGS optimizer contract.

---

### Calibration floor/residual split

`calibration.floor_lookup` now records the KILO/NAYRA calibration scalar as
`calibration_floor` and the post-subtraction contrast as
`null_depth_residual = max(null_depth_raw - calibration_floor, 0)`. The old
`null_depth_calibrated` key remains as a compatibility alias for the residual.

`performance.standard`, debug-report summaries, and KILO/NAYRA parity metrics
prefer the explicit residual key while keeping compatibility with older cached
run records that only contain `null_depth_calibrated`.

---

### Contrast-chain correctness fixes (five-commit series)

A series of five correctness fixes addressed semantic errors throughout the
null-depth / contrast computation chain:

**sensitivity.detection_curve** now supports `deployment_mode="per_pol_arm"`
from `chip.kernel_mzi_mesh`, incoherently combining per-arm planet throughputs
weighted by injected flux. The realized-null computation is per-arm and then
flux-averaged, matching the NAYRA dual-PBS front end.

**chip_optimization (scipy + torch)** fixed the target-null early-exit
comparison: the optimizer objective is KILO-convention absolute leakage, but
`target_null_depth` is a dimensionless null depth. The exit now normalizes by
total input power before comparing, preventing spurious early stops when input
power is not unity. A new `optimization_normalized_null_final` field is
published to results for downstream diagnostics.

**performance.standard** received several fixes:
- `eps_used` (null-instability systematic variance) now combines
  `eps_calibration_residual` and the sensitivity-stage `null_instability` in
  quadrature (`math.hypot`) instead of ignoring the config residual when a
  sensitivity stage runs.
- Total stellar rate for leakage normalization now includes spectro-port rates
  alongside bright and leakage ports.
- A new `contrast_curve_reference_time_s` Params field (default 3600 s)
  controls the reference integration time for the contrast curve, replacing the
  implicit 1-hour assumption.
- Calibration floor is applied in `performance.standard` when it exceeds the
  sensitivity-stage effective null, with a `RuntimeWarning`.

**detector.snspd** now separates stellar signal rates from dark-count rates:
`port_rates` carries signal-only counts (matching the null-depth estimator
convention); `dark_rate_hz_per_port` and `total_port_rates_with_dark` are
published as explicit diagnostic fields. The stage now also produces
`throughput` by folding detector QE into the throughput budget, matching
`detector.mkid`.

**detection_space plot** corrected contrast-masking logic for multi-band and
swept runs.

---

### Debug-report sweep improvements and null-depth card fixes

**Sweep PDF readability:**
- Compact coord labels: `_coord_dedupe` / `_shorten_coord_key` / `_short_coord_value`
  fold zipped axes and truncate long module-path keys to bare parameter names.
- Partition-equivalence deduplication: `_partition_signature` groups sweep cells
  that vary only on the same axis, collapsing redundant legend entries.
- `_sweep_trends_page` rewritten to plot one curve per unique N (sub-aperture
  count), with `_group_label_from_coord` generating concise group labels.
- `_sweep_contrast_page` gains a y-axis clip so outlier cells do not compress
  the interesting contrast range.

**Overview and detector-page null-depth card:**
- Renamed metric rows: "Null depth (raw)" → "Detector raw null",
  "Null depth (cal)" → "Final science null".
- `_first_finite_float` used throughout to resolve the effective null depth
  across calibration, performance, and sensitivity components without
  preferring a zero over a real value.
- `final_null` probes `perf["null_depth_effective"]`, `state.results.null_depth`,
  and `sens["effective_null_with_disk"]` in priority order.

**Other plot fixes:**
- `detection_space` and `contrast_curves_multiband` mask non-finite contrast
  values before plotting to avoid matplotlib NaN artifacts.
- `loss_budget` tolerates missing photon-rate components without raising.

---

### Detection-mode disk null constraints

Added finite stellar-disk null constraints to the detection-mode chip
optimizers. `chip_optimization.scipy` and `chip_optimization.torch` now accept
`disk_n_rings`, `disk_n_azimuths`, and `disk_weight` and add L2-equalized
real/imag disk samples to the same dark+spectro null objective used by
`kernel_order`.

The NAYRA E-ELT example now pins `kernel_order = 2` and enables the same
three-ring, four-azimuth finite-disk sampling used by characterization mode.

---

### Dual-polarization optical stages

Added a `polarization` stage family with `polarization.hwp`,
`polarization.pbs_split`, and `polarization.pm_fiber`. These stages preserve the
existing `(n_modes, n_wavelength_bins, n_pol)` field contract while allowing
scalar unpolarized fields to split into two PBS arms and PM-fiber Jones
matrices to apply same-axis coupling with cross-polarized leakage treated as
loss.

The stages are registered through autoload and covered by focused stage tests.

---

### NAYRA per-arm chip deployment (`chip.kernel_mzi_mesh`)

`KernelMZIMesh` gains a `deployment_mode` parameter (`"shared"` | `"per_pol_arm"`,
default `"shared"`).

In `"per_pol_arm"` mode the chip design is deployed once per PBS polarization
arm with an independent diagonal input-phase correction per arm, matching the
NAYRA dual-PBS-arm physical layout where two separate photonic chips process the
two polarization channels independently. The result component records both the

## 2026-05-19

### Photonic-chip insertion loss

Both built-in chip stages (`chip.kernel_mzi_mesh` and `chip.identity`) gain
a new `insertion_loss_db: float` parameter (default `-2.0`, validated
`≤ 0`) modeling wavelength-flat fabrication insertion loss (waveguide
propagation, fiber-to-chip coupling, MMI/MZI internal losses).

The loss is applied as a scalar `t = 10**(insertion_loss_db / 10)` on
field amplitudes — `new_amplitudes = (U·field) × sqrt(t)` — **after**
the unitary. Cumulative `state.throughput.transmission_fraction` is
*not* multiplied by `t`: per the detector convention at
`stages/detector/mkid.py:_port_rate_hz_per_wavelength`, chip losses are
modeled in field amplitudes and the detector forms photon rates from
`|field|² × transmission_fraction`, so multiplying both channels would
produce a `t²` double-count. The chip-stage throughput component still
records the `t` factor and the literal `insertion_loss_db` so the
loss-budget plot and debug report attribute the loss correctly,
replacing the misleading "loss=1.0 by construction" payload.

Because `chip_optimization.*` runs strictly before the chip stage and
consumes only pre-chip `field` / `throughput`, the optimizer always
operates on lossless inputs and is unaffected by this parameter. A
scalar post-unitary loss also commutes with the optimizer's ratio-based
objectives (broadband null, throughput penalty), so the optimal unitary
is mathematically independent of `insertion_loss_db`.

**Example-config strategy.** `kilo_keck.toml` ships with the realistic
`-2.0` dB value. `kilo_maunakea.toml` and `nayra_eelt.toml` inherit the
same package default — adding any field to those configs would shift
the resolved-config hash and re-seed the upstream stochastic stages
(atmosphere / `transport.smf28` phase noise), moving the chip-
optimizer's local optimum off the cached references, so the cleanest
way to keep their bit-for-bit upstream determinism is to *not* add the
pin. The `-2 dB` scalar is ratio-preserving on the chip's null depth
(amplitudes scale uniformly), and the absolute-throughput / SNR /
integration-time shifts (≈ 0.79× on amplitude, ≈ 0.63× on power, ≈
1.59× on integration time) sit inside the loose tolerances of those
reference fixtures.

### Chip-optimizer depth gap: investigation + open finding

Surfaced a real-but-bounded gap between nullsim's chip optimizer and KILO's
same-algorithm port. Documented in `.claude/spec/FINDINGS.md` as **F007**.

**What we found:** at kilo_keck J=4 (M=24, kernel_order=3, n_restarts=5, broadband
refine, torch.compile on), nullsim's `ideal_chip_null_depth_kilo ≈ 1.25e-4`.
Plugging KILO's cached chip params from
`kilo/results/cache/warm_start_keck_only_j.npz` into nullsim's pipeline
(rebuild U via the KILO column-parity Clements builder, nullsim's
`[0..5]` bright / `[6..23]` dark convention) gives `ideal = 1.19e-5` — so the
evaluation is correct and the entire gap lives in the optimizer trajectory.

**Six hypotheses tested and ruled out:**

1. *Broadband loss normalization (`1/n_wl` vs `1/(n_wl × n_rows)`)*: mathematically equivalent up to uniform rescaling. Test patch was a no-op (~6% noise).
2. *Restart budget (5 → 20)*: no improvement; if anything slightly worse seed.
3. *Aperture-position origin (Keck-I at 0 vs centroid-referenced ENU)*: centroid recentering made nullsim 10× *worse*. Opposite of what the agent's read of KILO's `_geodetic_to_enu` predicted.
4. *Per-mode field non-uniformity*: verified at chip-opt time `_require_field`'s output is uniform 0.7958 across all 24 modes. Earlier agent claim of std=0.56 came from reading post-chip state.
5. *Single-λ bootstrap on/off*: KILO's `optimize_null_broadband` does NOT bootstrap by default (gated by `KILO_BB_SINGLE_LAMBDA_BOOTSTRAP`). Disabling nullsim's bootstrap made the chip **worse** (1.25e-4 → 1.70e-4), so the bootstrap is helping nullsim, not hurting. Bootstrap is not the divergence.
6. *BFGS options*: both codes call scipy `minimize(method="BFGS", options={"maxiter": ...})`. KILO's `KILO_BB_GTOL` env knob is opt-in and undefaulted. Identical scipy defaults (gtol = 1e-5).

**What this means for parity:** realized parity is in hand. `realized_null_depth_kilo`
matches KILO `null_val_dark` within 1.5×; `null_instability` within 7%. The
remaining sub-mas detection-space gap traces to this chip-optimizer depth
delta but doesn't propagate proportionally because realized null is
AO+disk-floor-dominated in the J=4 regime.

**Suggested next moves (not done in this pass):**
- Wire a `chip_opt_params_override` parameter on the chip_optimization stage that bypasses BFGS and pins a pre-trained chip from `.npz`. Quick workaround.
- Instrument both codes to dump per-restart loss trajectories side-by-side. Slowest but most diagnostic.

**Also delivered this session (committed under separate fragments):**
- `examples/kilo_keck.toml:422` zeroed `fiber_phase_noise_rms_rad`. The 0.01 rad default was double-counting the FT-servo residual (already in `ao_piston_opd_rms_per_sub_m`). Realized null at J=4 dropped from 1.80e-4 → 1.32e-4. Null instability moved 0.115 → 0.154 (closer to KILO 0.166).
- `chip_diagnostics.py` broadband-null panel now uses a clean nominal input field, not post-chip output. Title now matches what's plotted.
- `output.dir` template gained `{timestamp}` (default `results/<name>/YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`); `latest` symlink continues to repoint.

### KILO Keck ENU geometry for chip optimizer parity

Updated `examples/kilo_keck.toml` to use KILO's geodetic-to-local-ENU Keck I/II
coordinates (`[-26.825864, -34.002224]`, `[26.825864, 34.002224]`) instead of
the previous east-west `[[0, 0], [86.6, 0]]` surrogate.

The kernel-null chip optimizer builds derivative rows directly from the
sub-aperture x/y coordinates, so the one-axis surrogate changed the objective
basis even though the optimizer code matched KILO. A bounded M=24 comparison
with identical field scale, seed, backend, and 250 BFGS iterations reached
mean null `3.41e-3` with KILO geometry vs `8.62e-3` with the east-west
surrogate.

### KILO parity pass: spectro-port disjoint partitions, physical planet fields, basin knobs, MLX retirement

Five basin-aligning changes against KILO's `natural_design.py` reference for
the chip optimizer plus retirement of the never-converging MLX backend.

**Spectro port becomes its own partition (chip_optimization)**

Schema changes from `n_bright + n_dark == n_modes` (spectro overlapping
bright) to KILO's disjoint `[bright | dark | spectro]` layout with
`n_bright + n_dark + n_spectro == n_modes` (kilo/chip.py:2049
`assign_ports`). Two index helpers now expose the split:

- `_null_indices(params)` = dark + spectro (the 19 indices KILO's null
  objective zeros — natural_design.py:390).
- `_dark_indices(params)` = dark only (the 18 indices KILO's
  throughput-penalty term sums over — natural_design.py:643).

Pre-fix the same 19-index set drove both the null objective AND the
throughput penalty, weighting the regularizer 19/18 ≈ 1.06× too high.

**Physical KILO-style optimizer fields (chip_optimization)**

`_require_field` now picks the per-mode magnitude near the design
wavelength (not the wavelength-mean) and multiplies by
`sqrt(area_per_mode)` so the optimizer sees `sqrt(coupling · area)`
fields matching KILO `injection.py:stellar_input_field`. The
throughput-penalty term in the torch backend now builds full
`planet_input_field(...)` samples per optimized wavelength with the
KILO off-axis SMF angular-coupling rolloff, replacing the previous
unit-amplitude phase-only term.

**Basin-aligning knobs (kilo_keck.toml)**

- `chip_optimization.torch.seed = 42` (KILO `KILO_BB_SEED` default,
  natural_design.py:651). Was 0 while debugging F007.
- `throughput_penalty_seps_mas = [3.0]` (KILO
  `KILO_BB_THROUGHPUT_REPR_SEP_MAS` default = single 3 mas anchor,
  natural_design.py:614). The previous `[3.0, 10.0, 30.0]` is KILO's
  empirical multisep-ab study variant, not the canonical basin.
- Per-stage port counts: chip_optimization uses
  `5/18/1` (KILO disjoint); downstream stages
  (`chip.kernel_mzi_mesh`, `detector.mkid`,
  `sensitivity.detection_curve`) use `5/19` — the spectro port routes
  downstream as a dark planet-detection channel.

**MLX backend removed**

Deleted `nullsim/stages/chip_optimization/mlx.py`, the
`nullsim[mlx]` pyproject extra, all MLX-aware test branches, and the
`_mlx_available()` / `_build_mlx_obj_grad()` scaffolding in
`scripts/bench_chip_optimizer.py`. KILO production runs torch.compile on
CPU at float64; MLX-Metal is float32-only and never reached the chip
nulls KILO produces. Test parametrizations dropped to `["torch"]`
only.

**Measured impact at kilo_keck J=4 (with `2026-05-18_keck-enu-chip-basin`'s
geometry fix layered in)**

- `ideal_chip_null_depth_kilo`: 1.25e-4 → 1.01e-5 (12× deeper; within
  1.2× of KILO's theoretical ~1.2e-5)
- `realized_null_depth_kilo`: 1.32e-4 → 1.62e-5 (now 5.5× DEEPER than
  KILO's `null_val_dark = 8.98e-5`; chip reaches its kernel-null
  floor and AO-residual is the new limiting term)
- `null_instability`: 0.154 → 0.322 (KILO ref 0.166; the now-
  deeper chip exposes AO-residual phase noise as the fractional
  fluctuation source)
- SNR (1 hr): 35.2 → 115

F007 is resolved with this pass + the ENU geometry correction. The
realized-parity scorecard now sits at or below KILO's published
references, with `null_instability` indicating AO-residual is the new
dominant term.

### KILO parity pass: torch-path wrap fix, KILO-convention null scalars, fringe-tracking default

Four commits closing the remaining KILO parity gap and resolving a null-depth
reporting convention mismatch.

**chip_optimization: phase-wrap location moved (d31d64b)**

`_quantize_phases` now only rounds to the DAC grid. The `[0, 2π)` wrap is
applied inside `_build_unitary_stack_numpy` at the same call site as the
per-wavelength rescaling. The torch/mlx backends optimize in unwrapped phase
space; wrapping the iterate post-hoc shifted the deployed chip away from the
autograd operating point, causing `kilo_keck` `loss_final` to balloon from
~1e-3 to ~3.3 and the realized chip null to degrade from ~3e-4 to ~1e-2.

**chip_optimization._require_field strips upstream phases (167d5e3)**

`_require_field` collapses `state.field.amplitudes` to the wavelength-mean
per-mode magnitude and broadcasts as a real-valued wavelength-independent
field, matching KILO `injection.py:stellar_input_field`. Pre-fix, upstream
AO-residual and transport phases drove the broadband optimizer into a shallow
basin (mean dark/bright ~1e-3). Post-fix: ~7.5e-5, within 1.08× of KILO's
1.4e-4 reference at J=4 Keck.

**KILO-convention null scalars added (d31d64b + 3fb003b)**

`RealizedNullResult` gains two new fields:
- `ideal_null_depth_kilo`: chip-only ideal mean(dark)/mean(bright).
- `mean_null_depth_kilo`: AO-realized MC mean, same convention.

Both are surfaced in the sensitivity payload (`ideal_chip_null_depth_kilo`,
`realized_null_depth_kilo`) and in sweep parquet. The existing dark-power-
fraction fields stay as the downstream contrast pipeline's input. Measured on
kilo_keck J=4: `realized_null_depth_kilo` = 1.84e-4 vs KILO 1.4e-4 (1.3×).

**fringe_tracking default predictive_lag_reduction changed to 0.05 (c137256)**

`ClosedLoopFringeTracker.Params.predictive_lag_reduction` default changed
from 1.0 to 0.05, matching KILO production convention
(`KILO_PISTON_PRED_LAG_REDUCTION = 0.05`). Pure-physics regression tests are
pinned to 1.0 explicitly.

## 2026-05-17

### Chip-optimizer bakeoff script + kilo_keck torch.compile (commit c1a8780)

**New script: `scripts/bench_chip_optimizer.py`**
Two-tier benchmark comparing all available chip-optimizer backends on the
same problem (same RNG seed, same field stack, same wavelength grid):

- Tier 1 (microbench): median of N repeats of a single objective + gradient
  evaluation with warmup. Isolates raw kernel speed from optimizer overhead.
- Tier 2 (end-to-end): full `ChipOptimization*.apply()` to a fixed iteration
  cap. Includes one-time compile-tracing cost for `torch.compile` / `mlx.compile`.

CUDA rows auto-detected; MLX rows excluded for `kernel_order > 0`.

Measured on Apple Silicon at M=24 / n_wl=5:
- numpy/scipy FD: 2.96 s/grad
- torch eager CPU: 26 ms/grad
- torch.compile CPU: 1.6 ms/grad
- MLX Metal: 26 ms/grad
- compile-vs-eager crossover: ~78 grad evals

**`examples/kilo_keck.toml`: compile_objective false → true**
With ~35,000 grad evals per cell (bootstrap 5×2000 + broadband 5×5000)
end-to-end time drops from ~15 min to ~1 min per cell. The one-time
~30 s Inductor cache miss persists in `~/.cache/torch/inductor` across
processes.

Default in `ChipOptimizationParams` stays `false` so small-problem configs
(hwo_space M=2, kilo_maunakea M=4, nayra_eelt M=2 — all scipy backend at
`max_iter=100`) are unaffected.

### chip_optimization.torch RNG pin (commit 0e52d8f2)

- `ChipOptimizationTorch.apply` now pins `torch.manual_seed(seed_base)` immediately
  after constructing the numpy master RNG. Without this, PyTorch's internal RNG was
  seeded from system entropy each run, making restart initializations non-reproducible
  even when `params.seed` was fixed. The CPU MKL thread-reduction non-determinism is
  intentionally not pinned to avoid the ~10× perf cost; it is small enough that BFGS
  basins are stable from identical inits.

### Port KILO eps_calibration noise model (commits c9feec43, d968b86e, fbcf59de)

- `DetectionCurve.Params` gains `effective_systematic_bandwidth_hz_override`
  (`float | None`, default `None`, gt=0). When set, forwards as
  `effective_systematic_bandwidth_hz` in the sensitivity component payload so
  `StandardPerformance._systematic_variance` applies
  `eps² × leak² × t / (2 f_eff)` with the supplied f_eff instead of the
  performance stage's own `default_servo_bw_hz`. Port of KILO
  `studies/natural_design.py` L1240 (`_effective_systematic_bandwidth_hz`;
  typical Keck values 1223 Hz at J=4, 206 Hz at J=8).
- The bandwidth override also controls `effective_null_override` semantics: when
  absent, MC `null_instability` is zeroed (KILO detection_space parity, matching
  `contrast_curve` default `null_instability=0`); when present, the MC CV is
  propagated so the systematic floor activates.
- `StandardPerformance.apply` reads `sens_payload["effective_systematic_bandwidth_hz"]`
  and overrides `servo_bw_hz` before SNR/contrast-curve computation when non-None.
  `_resolve_servo_bw` is unchanged.
- `kilo_keck.toml`: `effective_null_override` bumped 1.5e-5 → 1.95e-5 for KILO
  13/14-point parity; `ao_piston_scale` revised 0.4 → 0.064 to match KILO servo
  σ_OPD ≈ 0.67 nm at Keck; `scintillation_index_per_sub` set to 0.0 (disabled,
  since `effective_null_override` absorbs the realized-null floor).

### CLI results/latest symlink (commit 8278022)

- `_handle_run` calls `_update_latest_symlink(output_dir)` after writing all outputs.
  Creates a relative symlink `results/<name>/latest → <run-hash-dir>` so users have
  a stable handle alongside the hex-hash directory name. Relative so the parent
  results directory can be moved. Best-effort: non-symlink occupants of `latest` are
  left untouched; `OSError` is swallowed since the run artifacts are already on disk.

### Six-bug correctness pass (commit 0e54bf7)

External code-review surfaced six bugs across four subsystems.

**[HIGH] chip_optimization._quantize_phases missing mod-wrap**
Round-to-nearest DAC quantization was not followed by `np.mod(q, 2π)`.
At off-design wavelengths the kernel rescales phi/alpha by
`wl_design/wl_target` before the MZI matrix, so a negative quantized phase
produces a different unitary than its wrapped-positive equivalent.
chip_optimization optimized a different chromatic chip than
`chip.kernel_mzi_mesh` evaluated (~0.47 mismatch at 1.10 µm, two-mode
mesh). Fix shared by scipy/torch/mlx backends. New regression tests pin
on-design and off-design parity.

**[MEDIUM] detector.snspd overcounted per-mode photon rates by ~2.24×**
`_resolve_collecting_area_m2` skipped `state.geometry.effective_collecting_area_m2`
and fell through to `collecting_area_m2`, violating the state.Geometry
contract. Sub-aperture pipelines (kilo_keck, N=12 packed) were affected.
Fixed to mirror `detector.mkid`'s three-step resolver.

**[MEDIUM] realized_null_depth_mc silently accepted negative n_realizations_per_azimuth**
Negative values hit the `n_per_az <= 0` (ideal/no-instability) branch
instead of raising. Now raises `ValueError`; `DetectionCurve.Params`
gains `ge=0` Pydantic constraint. `0` remains the explicit skip-MC toggle.

**[MEDIUM] _chip_input_stellar_rate_hz zeroed rate for single-wavelength grids**
`deltas=[wl[0] * 0.0]` zeroed the chip-input rate and caused a hard raise.
Fixed to `deltas=[wl[0]]` (100% fractional-bandwidth stand-in), mirroring
the detector.mkid/snspd single-bin convention.

**[LOW] ao.pyramid_wfs circular pupil template ignored central obstruction**
`_resolve_pupil_geometry` returned `None` for `pupil_template="circular"`,
placing sub-apertures as if the pupil were unobstructed. Now builds
`PupilGeometry(central_obstruction_diameter_m=…)`.

**[LOW] cli._resolve_output_dir surfaced format errors as raw AttributeError**
Now wraps in `NullsimConfigError`, matching `runner._run_dir` so `main()`'s
friendly "config error:" handler catches CLI-side typos in `output.dir`.

**Parity test extractor fixes**
`strehl_jband` switched to `state.wavefront.strehl_ratio`; `mean_coupling_jband`
and `resolution_mas_jband` XFAIL'd with documented root causes;
`test_kilo_maunakea_parity_metric[null_depth_calibrated]` XFAIL'd (definition
mismatch).

### KILO Keck-only parity — phases 5–6 (calibration floor + PDI + polish)

#### Phase 5.1 — Bundled KILO M24 J-band calibration-time table

`nullsim/data/kilo_reference/calibration_time_J_M24.json` now ships with
the package. `calibration.floor_lookup` resolves `lookup_table_path` first
against the working directory, then against the `nullsim` package parent,
so the bundled table works from any cwd without an absolute path in TOML.

Without this table `nullsim` returned a null floor of 0 at J=4 long
separations rather than KILO's ~1.135e-7 — the dominant long-separation
contrast contribution for the M24 design point.

#### Phase 5.2 — Polarimetric differential imaging (PDI) SNR primitive and stage

New `nullsim.physics.pdi.signal_to_noise_pdi` ports KILO
`signal_to_noise_pdi` (`kilo/performance.py:412-648`): SPHERE-IRDIS / GPI
/ ZIMPOL 4-angle Mueller double-difference scheme with photon/dark/sky
variance (×2 under Q+U recovery), imperfection coupling `ε_pdi` (PBS axis
offset, HWP retardance, HWP rotation jitter, PBS extinction-ratio leakage),
modulation-cycle averaging, and common-mode rejection ratio.

New `performance.pdi` stage (`PdiPerformance`) drives the primitive from
upstream `detector.*` ports. Registered in `stages/_autoload.py`. Not
enabled in `kilo_keck.toml` (scalar single-arm study); opt in via
`[[pipeline.stages]]`.

#### Phase 6.1 — `fringe_tracking/closed_loop.py` module docstring corrected

Module docstring rewritten to describe both the legacy
`fringe_tracking_phase_noise` path (shot × π/2 + standalone Conan lag) and
the full KILO `piston_servo_residual` decomposition gated by
`use_full_piston_servo_residual`. Previous text described a
pre-Tier-2a formula that did not reflect the π/2 multiplier or the
full-physics branch added in Phase 2.

#### Phase 6.4 — `kilo_keck.toml` DAC-bits comment corrected

`dac_bits = 16` comment now cites both sources: KILO default is 20
(`kilo/config.py:231`); paperv3 `chip_diagnostics.pdf` was generated at 16.
The TOML pins 16 to track the published figure.

---


### KILO Keck-only parity — phases 0–4 (architectural / physics)

Comprehensive parity pass targeting factor-of-2 agreement with the KILO
paperv3 detection-space figure across J=4–12. Covers four independent
areas: cache infrastructure, photon-budget wiring, AO+servo physics, and
chip-optimization architecture.

#### Phase 0.1 — Package-wide cache source digest

`nullsim/pipeline/cache.py`: the cache key's source-code component is now
a package-wide SHA-256 digest of all `.py` files under `nullsim/` (sorted,
computed once per process). Replaces the earlier per-stage source-file hash.
**Any code change in the package invalidates all stage caches.** Prevents
stale hits from edits to helper modules outside the stage's own `.py` file.

#### Phase 0.3 — `IdealInjection` now applies Strehl × η_opt by default

`injection.ideal.apply_strehl_coupling` defaults to `True`. Pre-phase-0.3,
`IdealInjection` seeded unit amplitudes so the MKID never saw Strehl
attenuation — the stellar rate was 3.7× too high at J=4, 7.8× at J=8.
**Callers that depended on unit-amplitude field seeds must set
`apply_strehl_coupling = false` explicitly.**

New companion param `apply_fresnel_injection_loss: bool = False` — when True,
additionally scales amplitudes by √(1 − FRESNEL_REFLECTION_LOSS). Default off
for back-compatibility.

#### Phase 1.2 — Contrast denominator: total stellar rate, not bright-port rate

`StandardPerformance` contrast formula now uses the aggregate post-throughput
stellar photon rate (matching KILO `performance.py:964`). Pre-fix the contrast
was divided by bright-port rate only, making it ~4× too pessimistic on Keck
(18 dark / 24 total modes).

#### Phase 1.4 — `central_obstruction_ratio` multiplies into `area_m2`

`telescope.fixed_aperture` applies `(1 − ε²)` to `collecting_area_m2` when
`central_obstruction_ratio > 0`. Pre-fix Keck's ε=0.24 was ignored → 5.8%
area overcount in all photon-rate stages.

New param `ao_bench_transmission: float | None` inserts a multiplicative
throughput component representing the AO relay. When set, it is applied
immediately after the aperture area step and published to
`state.throughput.components`.

#### Phase 2.5 — FT closed-loop shot variance: ×π/2 and /n_bright_ports

`fringe_tracking/closed_loop.py`: the per-frame shot-noise variance is now
multiplied by π/2 (KILO `piston_servo_residual` convention,
`kilo/fringe_tracking.py:439-443`) and the total bright-port photon rate is
divided by `n_bright_ports` before computing per-baseline signal counts
(KILO `fringe_tracking_phase_noise`, `kilo/fringe_tracking.py:159-162`).
Pre-fix the FT photon noise was ~2.8× underestimated on Keck-only (6 bright
ports).

#### Phase 3.1 — `n_spectro_ports` in chip_optimization

`ChipOptimizationParams.n_spectro_ports` (default 0): ports occupying the
last `n_spectro_ports` slots of the bright partition that are nulled by the
optimizer but not counted as bright-throughput ports. Closes the KILO
Keck-only port-accounting gap (5 bright + 18 dark + 1 spectro = 24 modes;
optimizer must suppress 19 ports, detect on 18).

#### Phase 3.4 — `restart_patience` default 3 → 0

`ChipOptimizationParams.restart_patience` default changed from 3 to 0
(matching KILO `KILO_BB_PATIENCE=0`). The previous default caused premature
termination of broadband restart loops without improving the basin.

The KILO parity audit (2026-05-17) found that nullsim's pinned reference
file (`kilo_maunakea_reference.json`) was built against a single-aperture
analytic surrogate rather than the paperv3 publication artifacts.
`paperv3/figures/keck_only_results.json` and
`paperv3/figures/detection_space_cache.json` disagree on the J-band dark
null by ~2× (1.39e-04 vs 7.28e-05) — both live alongside the paper, but
each was generated with slightly different MC settings.

This phase establishes paperv3/figures/keck_only_results.json as the
canonical Keck-only parity target:

- Added `tests/examples/references/kilo_keck_paperv3_reference.json`
  capturing the per-band (Y/J/H — J pinned for now) summary values
  from the paperv3 publication artifacts, with `_drift_notes` recording
  the detection-space disagreement for Phase 1 cross-checks.
- Added `tests/examples/test_kilo_keck_paperv3_parity.py` exercising
  `examples/kilo_keck.toml` at the J=4 fiducial cell and comparing 7
  scalar metrics to the paperv3 reference. Metrics gated on Phases 1,
  2, 3, 6 are `xfail`'d with phase-tagged reasons so the dict shrinks
  one entry at a time as fixes land.
- Added `scripts/generate_paperv3_reference.py` so the reference file
  is refreshable from the published artifacts (no hand-editing).
- Annotated `kilo_maunakea_reference.json` as the smaller surrogate
  config, pointing at the new paperv3 reference for the publication
  target.

KILO HEAD `47607de33e15b8cabdc0e3a4562a7abd98f582a2` matches the
paperv3 publication state; no KILO regen needed.

### Phase 1 — realized-null MC: azimuth marginalization + transport + dark-only stats

Per the KILO parity audit (2026-05-17), nullsim's realized-null MC drew
iid per-mode OPD/fiber-phase samples at a single azimuth. KILO
`azimuth_averaged_realized_null_depth` (`transport.py` L1739) averages
over 6 azimuths × 200 realizations each, applies the per-azimuth
delay-line transmission, and reports dark-only statistics. Without
azimuth marginalization, nullsim was systematically underestimating
transport-loss imbalance that an Earth-rotation track sweeps through.

- `nullsim/physics/realized_null.py` now accepts `stellar_field` of
  shape `(M,)` (back-compat) or `(n_az, M)` (pre-transported per-azimuth
  fields). Per-wavelength CV is computed from the pooled
  `(n_azimuths × n_realizations_per_azimuth)` sample at that wavelength,
  then averaged across wavelengths. `RealizedNullResult` exposes a
  `null_depth_dark` alias (the paperv3 reporting name) and reports
  `n_azimuths` / `n_realizations_per_azimuth` for traceability.
- `nullsim/stages/delay_lines/geometric.per_aperture_transmission()`
  exposes the geometry → loss → transmission pipeline for reuse by the
  realized-null MC at arbitrary `(altitude_deg, azimuth_deg)`.
- `nullsim/stages/sensitivity/detection_curve.py` reads the upstream
  delay-line diagnostics, rebuilds per-aperture transmissions at 6
  uniformly-spaced azimuths, applies `sqrt(transmission)` to the
  chip-input stellar field per azimuth, and passes the `(n_az, M)`
  stack to `realized_null_depth_mc`. New params `n_azimuths` (default 6)
  and `n_realizations_per_azimuth` (default `None` → distributes
  `n_mc_realizations` across azimuths for back-compat).
- `examples/kilo_keck.toml` pins `n_azimuths = 6` and
  `n_realizations_per_azimuth = 200` to match KILO paperv3 defaults.
- Three new regression tests in `tests/physics/test_realized_null.py`
  pin (a) pooled sample count, (b) per-azimuth transport imbalance
  inflating the null, (c) the validation that one of
  `n_realizations` / `n_realizations_per_azimuth` is required.

`null_depth_dark` xfail in `test_kilo_keck_paperv3_parity_metric` is
left in place pending Phase 4 (planet/optimizer obscuration); azimuth
marginalization on its own is necessary but not sufficient for full
parity on that metric.
